beats.narration_en: Hit a flat wall at a shallow angle, and the car doesn't glance off, it just stops dead.
Along the highway, this low concrete wall running beside the lane is called a Jersey barrier.
This barrier's face isn't flat at all. It's cut at an angle, rising like a ramp.
A wheel that strikes that slope climbs up it, instead of digging straight into the concrete.
That small lift is enough to redirect the whole car, steering it back into its own lane.
One carefully angled curve in a concrete wall keeps cars from becoming out of control projectiles.
